column1: # doctrine/readme_routes.tsv — the routed-destination registry required by README_POLICY.md
# ("Routing pressure closure"). DATA ONLY: no prose, no derived values, no duplicated counts.
# Moving content out of the README is not enough if the destination becomes an unbounded
# neighbouring sink. Every destination the landing page routes to — as a reader's navigation
# target, or as an author's overflow target named by the guard's own failure hint — has a row
# here with a class, an owner, a pressure control, and where the class demands it, numeric
# ceilings. An unclassified destination is a failed adoption.
# columns:
#   destination        repo-root-relative path (a trailing / means a directory family)
#   route_class        reader_navigation | author_overflow | both
#   lifecycle          hot_live | partitioned | generated_index | append_history | frozen | normative
#   owner              what governs its size and lifecycle
#   health_lines       advisory target: LINES for a file, FILE COUNT for a directory family; 0 = ungoverned
#   health_bytes       advisory target: BYTES for a file, AGGREGATE BYTES for a family; 0 = ungoverned
#   ceiling_lines      enforced ceiling on the same axis as health_lines; 0 = ungoverned
#   ceiling_bytes      enforced ceiling on the same axis as health_bytes; 0 = ungoverned
#   ceiling_part_bytes directory families only: the largest single member may not exceed this.
#                      An aggregate bound alone permits one member to become the monolith the
#                      split was meant to avoid. 0 = ungoverned.
# A partitioned family's required control is a bounded index PLUS per-part, file-count and
# aggregate ceilings — splitting a monolith without bounding the collection moves the same
# append pressure one level down, and bounding only the aggregate lets one member become the
# monolith.
# ⭐ THE TWO LIFECYCLES CALIBRATE HEALTH TARGETS DIFFERENTLY, and conflating them is why the
# first cut produced noise. For a HOT/LIVE surface the health target sits just above today's
# reviewed size, because unexpected growth is the thing worth knowing about. For an
# APPEND_HISTORY surface it belongs near the CEILING, because growth is expected and the only
# useful warning is "the shard threshold is approaching". CHANGELOG.md was given 24 KiB health
# against a 64 KiB ceiling when it measured 16 KiB; it crossed that target within a day of
# ordinary work, which is a miscalibrated instrument, not a finding. Family measurements at adoption: docs/tasks/ 5 files / 39,131 B;
# docs/decisions/ 5 / 8,246; docs/knowledge/ 4 / 6,834; docs/book/ 3 / 947;
# docs/provenance/ 5 / 10,860. `docs/` itself stays ungoverned as an umbrella: every family
# inside it carries its own bound, and double-counting would make one row fire for another's
# growth. Its members are the terminals.
# ⛔ Ceilings are DERIVED from this project's own trimmed surfaces, never copied from another
# project. Raising one requires a reviewed decision that the surface's contract expanded.
# Re-derivation, UPSTREAM-TRACK.1 (2026-09-20), when the aggregate fired at 396,273 B over 393,216:
#   docs/tasks/  25 files / 396,273 B; largest member P0-PROFILE.md at 50,097 B. Raised to
#                health 32 / 320 KiB, ceiling 48 / 640 KiB. ⛔ PER-PART STAYS 64 KiB — the
#                aggregate answers "how many lanes does this project track", the per-part answers
#                "has one tree become a monolith", and only the first question changed. Grounds
#                and the rejected alternatives (compaction, a subdirectory that would have broken
#                FRONTIER-SYNC's flat link pattern) are in
#                docs/decisions/decision_task-tree-family-bound.md.
# Derivation, SOT-FORMAT.9, when this project became LinkedSpec's first downstream consumer:
#   docs/upstream/  23 files / 24 KiB at adoption, across 3 issues. Health 60 files / 256 KiB;
#                   ceiling 150 / 1 MiB; per-part 32 KiB. ⭐ THE AXIS IS FILE COUNT, not bytes: an
#                   issue is a directory of small files — a REPORT, a repro script, one file per
#                   case, captured evidence, a candidate patch — so eight or so files arrive per
#                   issue while none of them is large. The per-part bound is what a maintainer
#                   will read in one sitting, not what suits this repository.
#                   ⛔ Its `cases/*.sexp` are DELIBERATELY PATHOLOGICAL and are excluded from
#                   scripts/compare_readers.py's corpus sweep, with an arm proving it.
# Derivation, MODEL-METHOD.11, when the primary-source catalogue got a home:
#   materials/       1 file / 25,409 B at adoption (catalog.sexp, 22 materials + 2 measured gaps).
#                    Health 4 files / 64 KiB; ceiling 12 / 256 KiB; per-part 128 KiB. ⭐ The axis
#                    that moves here is BYTES PER FILE, not file count: a catalogue grows by
#                    material, and each material carries prose about what it supplies and why.
#                    So the per-part bound is the one that will bite, and when it does the right
#                    split is by corpus or by architecture family, not by date. Registered in the
#                    same commit that created the directory, for the reason the CHANGELOG shard
#                    records below.
#                    ⛔ `.materials/` — the fetched document cache — is NOT a routed destination
#                    and has no row: it is gitignored, holds no tracked content, and is rebuilt by
#                    `scripts/materials.py --fetch`. A registry row would claim the repository
#                    governs bytes it does not carry.
# Derivation, MODEL-COMPOSE.2, when reusable definition fragments got their own home:
#   definitions/     2 files / 10,074 B at adoption (riscv/rv64i.sexp, riscv/m.sexp). Health 12
#                    files / 128 KiB; ceiling 30 / 256 KiB; per-part 64 KiB. A fragment is one
#                    ISA base or one extension, so the FILE COUNT is the axis that will move —
#                    RISC-V alone has over a hundred ratified extensions — while any single
#                    fragment stays small. Registered in the same commit that created the
#                    directory, for the reason the CHANGELOG shard records below.
# Derivation, P0-PROFILE.8, when CHANGELOG.md crossed its 64 KiB ceiling and was sharded:
#   docs/changelog/  1 file / 35,480 B at adoption. Health 6 files / 192 KiB; ceiling 20 / 384 KiB;
#                    per-part 64 KiB — the SAME per-part bound CHANGELOG.md itself carries, so a
#                    shard that grows past it is sharded again rather than becoming a new monolith.
#                    ⛔ Registered in the same commit that created the directory: sharding a capped
#                    file into an UNGOVERNED neighbour is the exact failure this registry exists to
#                    prevent, and it would have looked like a fix.
# Re-derivation, SEMULITH-TREES.4, measured once the roadmap conversion made the corpus final:
#   LIVE_STATUS.md     36 lines / 3,297 B  -> health 45 / 4 KiB (it gains a row per milestone)
#   docs/TASK_TREE.md  68 lines / 4,277 B  -> health 85 / 5 KiB (one row per ACTIVE tree)
#   CHANGELOG.md      352 lines / 25,814 B -> health 48 KiB: 75% of its 64 KiB shard threshold
#   DEV_NOTES.md       50 lines /  3,759 B -> health 36 KiB: 75% of its 48 KiB shard threshold
#   docs/tasks/        17 files / 133,074 B, largest member SEMULITH-PKG.md at 35,395 B
#                      -> health 24 files / 192 KiB; ceiling 40 / 384 KiB; per-part 64 KiB.
#                      Eleven milestone trees will each grow as their leaves gain evidence —
#                      SEMULITH-PKG.md reached 35 KiB with seven leaves archived — so the
#                      per-part ceiling is the one that actually bites, and it bites on the
#                      right thing: a tree whose archive should be compacted or split.
# Derivation, SEMULITH-PKG.4, measured on the trimmed surfaces:
#   README.md         67 lines / 3,719 B -> ceiling ~1.27x lines, ~1.31x bytes. Its health was
#                      first set AT today's size and fired on the very next row added (68 lines
#                      / 3,820 B, P0-PROFILE.1) — the same miscalibration this header warns
#                      about, committed in the file that warns about it. Re-set to 78 / 4,352,
#                      between the reviewed page and its untouched ceiling.
#   MEMORY.md         24 lines / 1,380 B -> health ~1.25x; ceiling stays the layer-A contract (50/7168)
#   LIVE_STATUS.md    33 lines / 2,066 B -> health ~1.36x; ceiling ~2.7x (it gains a row per milestone)
#   docs/TASK_TREE.md 52 lines / 2,651 B -> health ~1.25x; ceiling ~2.1x (one row per ACTIVE tree only)
#   CHANGELOG.md     222 lines / 16,228 B -> health 24 KiB; ceiling 64 KiB, then shard
#   DEV_NOTES.md      50 lines /  3,759 B -> health 12 KiB; ceiling 48 KiB, then shard
#   KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md  39 lines /  2,418 B -> derived file; health 8 KiB, ceiling 32 KiB
# A health target set AT today's size fires on the next line and teaches its reader to ignore
# it; these sit a deliberate band below their ceiling instead.
# Derivation, ARTIFACT-CLEANUP.1, when the §8 cleanup record got its home:
#   docs/ARTIFACT_CLEANUP.md  4 lines / 470 B at adoption. Health 6 / 768; ceiling 12 / 1,536.
#                    One overwrite-only entry per cleanup — history would defeat its purpose
#                    (the file exists to say when the LAST run happened), so the ceilings are
#                    pure guard rails against accidental append. Registered in the same commit
#                    that created it.
# Derivation, SOT-FORMAT.1, when the schema language got its home:
#   schema/          1 file / 2,180 B at adoption (schema.sexp — the language in itself). Health
#                    4 files / 64 KiB; ceiling 12 / 256 KiB; per-part 64 KiB — the SAME shape as
#                    definitions/: a schema is one file per construct family, and the family
#                    grows by construct the way definitions/ grows by fragment. Registered in the
#                    same commit that created the directory.
# Re-derivation, SOT-FORMAT.4, when the schema layer became the home of every dossier family:
#   schema/          12 files / 34,072 B (schema.sexp the fixpoint + one schema per corpus
#                    family: encoding, fragment, semantics, requirements, contract-obligations,
#                    profile, state, sources, references, override, expectations). Health 16
#                    files / 128 KiB; ceiling 24 / 512 KiB; per-part STAYS 64 KiB. Grounds: the
#                    director's one-format decision (2026-09-14) is the surface's contract
#                    expanding — the dossier moved behind the layer, so its six construct
#                    families each gained a schema, the same shape as the records at `.3`.
#                    The per-part axis is unchanged: one schema stays one family's grammar,
#                    readable in a sitting. This is the docs/tasks/ precedent: an expanded
#                    contract re-derives the count axis, never the per-part one.
#destination
